description: Execute Bean 0097 in holon-coherence: fix prompt prefill throughput reporting 0.00 tok/s, stop non-streaming requests from corrupting decode throughput with physically impossible 34k-38k tok/s values, guard throughput math against near-zero durations, and audit every telemetry metric for mathematical consistency across CumulativeMetrics, /holon/api/metrics, the web dashboard, the CLI scorecard and the offline wire-log parser
goal: Implement and verify changes across holon-coherence for Bean 0097: 1) PREFILL THROUGHPUT NEVER REPORTS ZERO (mitm_addon.py, commands/metrics.py): prefill_tps must equal prompt tokens divided by a genuine TTFT in seconds whenever prompt tokens > 0 and TTFT > 0. Audit every endpoint family (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible) so ttft is captured from the real request start and the real first-token/first-payload arrival, never defaulted to now (which yields ttft = 0.0 and prefill 0.00 tok/s). Guard against missing or zero request_start_time / response_headers_time / first_chunk_time by leaving the sample unmeasured instead of recording 0.0, so avg_prefill_throughput_tps, latest_prefill_tps, avg_tail_prefill_tps and latest_tail_prefill_tps stay faithful in CumulativeMetrics, /holon/api/metrics, holon-coherence metrics and _read_offline_metrics. 2) DECODE THROUGHPUT ONLY FROM GENUINE STREAMING (mitm_addon.py): stop computing output_tps as output_tokens / (total_time - ttft) for non-streaming responses, because headers and the full body arrive in the same network chunk so generation_time collapses to socket parse time (~0.001s) and yields absurd 34,000-38,000 tok/s values that poison the cumulative average. Compute decode throughput exclusively from real SSE chunk intervals (first_chunk_time to last_chunk_time), require a streaming response flag, and treat generation durations below a realistic 0.05s floor as unmeasured rather than as samples. Expose decode throughput as null/unmeasured for those requests and keep avg_decode_throughput_tps and latest_decode_throughput_tps averages over valid streaming samples only. 3) FULL METRIC CONSISTENCY AUDIT (mitm_addon.py, commands/metrics.py): verify total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, total_cache_read_tokens, total_cache_creation_tokens, total_reasoning_tokens, provider_cache_hit_rate (cache_read / total_input), cache_hit_rate (cache_hits / total_requests), tool_calls_pruned (tool_outputs_omitted), tokens_reduced, chars_saved, avg_ttft_ms (sum_ttft_ms / count_ttft), avg_prefill_throughput_tps, latest_prefill_tps, avg_tail_prefill_tps, latest_tail_prefill_tps, avg_decode_throughput_tps and latest_decode_throughput_tps are computed with identical formulas, identical zero/None guards and identical rounding in the live in-memory proxy, the /holon/ dashboard, the terminal scorecard and the offline wire-log parser. 4) TESTS: add comprehensive unit tests in tests/test_mitm_addon.py and tests/test_cli.py asserting exact prefill and decode tok/s for streaming and non-streaming responses, asserting non-streaming requests never enter the decode average, asserting sub-50ms generation windows are rejected, asserting missing-timing samples do not produce 0.00 prefill, and asserting live and offline metric aggregation agree. 5) VERIFICATION: keep uv run task lint and uv run task test fully green.

questions.question: Should decode throughput be reported as 0.00 for non-streaming requests or omitted entirely?
questions.answer: Omitted. Non-streaming decode throughput is physically meaningless, so the per-request value is reported as null/unmeasured and the request never contributes to avg_decode_throughput_tps.

questions.question: What streaming duration floor should reject unreliable decode samples?
questions.answer: 0.05 seconds, matching the acceptance criteria in Bean 0097.

questions.question: May the fix change the JSON contract of /holon/api/metrics?
questions.answer: Only additively. Existing keys keep their names and semantics; unmeasured throughput values become null instead of a fabricated float.

description: Execute Bean 0130 in holon-coherence: fix proxy readiness race condition during cold start by polling HTTP metrics endpoint instead of host TCP port, and add agent runner startup integration tests.
goal:
1) FIX PROXY READINESS: In src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, update wait_for_proxy_ready to actively poll http://127.0.0.1:{port}/holon/api/metrics (or /_holon/metrics) with urllib.request instead of only checking is_port_in_use. Ensure it verifies HTTP 200 from mitmproxy, catches URLError/ConnectionRefusedError/OSError, retries until timeout (PROXY_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), and fails fast if the container stops running.
2) UNIT TESTS: Update TestWaitForProxyReady in tests/test_cli.py to verify HTTP polling behaviour: success on HTTP 200, retries on initial connection failure before succeeding, fail-fast when container exits, and timeout handling.
3) INTEGRATION TESTS: Add integration tests in tests/test_agent_startup.py (marked with @pytest.mark.integration_test) verifying cold-start execution of supported agent runners (holon-coherence agy, pi, claude, codex, opencode) using -- --help or dry-run, ensuring the proxy container is booted automatically without connection drops or unexpected EOF.

description: Two holon-coherence changes in one execution: (Bean 0129) expose the plain mitmweb request/response inspection dashboard by default from 'holon-coherence start' with host port-conflict fallback and print every exposed endpoint (proxy, Coherence live dashboard, mitmweb inspector with its access token) from 'status', 'metrics' and 'start' output; (Bean 0133) measure the proxy readiness poll deadline with a monotonic clock so a wall-clock step can neither stretch nor short-circuit cold-start readiness.
goal:
1) BEAN 0133 - MONOTONIC READINESS DEADLINE: in src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, wait_for_proxy_ready() currently computes 'deadline = time.time() + timeout' and loops on 'while time.time() < deadline', while sibling loops in the same module already use time.monotonic(). Convert the deadline computation and the loop bound to time.monotonic() so the timeout is a duration and not a wall-clock instant. Audit every other time.time() use in the package: convert any that measures an elapsed duration or a timeout deadline, and leave genuine epoch timestamps (log lines, wire records, telemetry timestamps) untouched. Add a regression test that drives the readiness poll with an injected fake clock and asserts (a) a backwards wall-clock step cannot extend the poll, (b) a forwards wall-clock step cannot short-circuit it while the endpoint is still refusing connections, and (c) the poll still returns as soon as the metrics endpoint answers HTTP 200. Follow the fake-clock test style already established for the HTTP readiness polling tests.
2) BEAN 0129 - MITMWEB INSPECTION UI BY DEFAULT: in src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py the mitmweb tool is only selected when '--web' is passed ('tool = "mitmweb" if args.web else "mitmdump"'), so a plain 'holon-coherence start' gives no way to inspect live traffic. Make the mitmweb inspector available without extra flags on a normal start, with a host port-conflict fallback for the inspector port (default 8081, overridable) mirroring the fallback behaviour already used for the proxy and dashboard ports, and keep an explicit opt-out switch so a headless start can still run mitmdump only. Preserve the existing token/password handling: resolve and persist the inspector password/token exactly as the '--web' path does today, pass it to mitmweb so the UI is not unauthenticated, and never print or log the token in a way that leaks it into wire logs. Keep the existing secret scrubbing patterns for logged requests and responses in place and verify they still apply to inspector output.
3) BEAN 0129 - ENDPOINT REPORTING: 'holon-coherence start', 'holon-coherence status' and 'holon-coherence metrics' must each print every exposed endpoint with its actually resolved host:port, namely the proxy listen address, the Coherence live dashboard (the custom metrics UI served under /holon/), and the plain mitmweb inspection URL in the exact form 'http://127.0.0.1:<web_port>/?token=<token>' with a label that makes clear this is raw request/response inspection. When the inspector is not running, say so explicitly instead of printing a stale URL. Keep the terminal table formatting conventions already used by 'metrics'.
4) TESTS: extend the unit tests so the new behaviour is covered without needing Docker: default start selects mitmweb and passes the resolved inspector port plus the token, the opt-out path still selects mitmdump, an occupied inspector port falls back to the next free port, the printed start/status/metrics output contains all three endpoints, and the readiness deadline is monotonic. All tests must run with 'uv run pytest' (integration tests stay marked so 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test"' passes without Docker). Never use synthetic or mock data to report metrics or benchmark numbers.
5) DOCS: update README.md and the relevant docs/ pages to explain how to open the mitmweb inspector to view live request methods, URLs, headers, request bodies, response status codes and bodies, cache status and TLS details, how the token is resolved and where it is printed, how to opt out, and how the endpoints and ports are reported by start/status/metrics.
6) QUALITY GATES: run 'make lint', 'uv run ruff check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test"' and make them pass with zero errors. Format any changed markdown with the repository's own configuration only. Use Australian English spelling in all comments, docstrings and log strings. No new runtime dependencies.

questions.question: Should the mitmweb inspector be enabled by default?
questions.answer: Yes, a plain 'holon-coherence start' must expose the mitmweb inspector on its default port with a port-conflict fallback and token authentication, while an explicit opt-out keeps the headless mitmdump-only behaviour.

questions.question: How must the inspector token be treated?
questions.answer: It must be resolved and persisted exactly as today, passed to mitmweb so the UI stays authenticated, and never written to wire logs or any unsanitised output.

questions.question: Which clock must bound the proxy readiness wait?
questions.answer: time.monotonic(), because the timeout is a duration. Wall-clock time.time() stays only for genuine epoch timestamps.

description: holon-coherence does not pin its interpreter: pyproject.toml:10 declares requires-python = ">=3.12", pyproject.toml:53 sets ruff target-version = "py311", uv.lock:3 records requires-python = ">=3.12", and there is no .python-version. 'uv sync' therefore resolves the newest interpreter on the host: on 2026-10-24 both a fresh worktree and an existing checkout's .venv came up on Python 3.14.8. Everything else already says 3.13: environment.yml:5 pins python=3.13.15, README.md:104 installs python=3.13 for the conda base route, and the sibling holon-agentic-coder pins requires-python "==3.13.*" with ruff py313. CI never selects a version: test-unit.yml:47 runs 'uv sync; uv run task test' with no python-version input, so a committed .python-version aligns CI without any workflow edit. Checked on main acbe924: ruff 0.16.7 with --target-version py313 reports 'All checks passed!' and '90 files already formatted', so the new target needs no source change.
goal:
1) pyproject.toml: requires-python = "==3.13.*" and [tool.ruff] target-version = "py313"; nothing else in the file changes.
2) Add .python-version containing 3.13.
3) Regenerate uv.lock with 'uv lock' so it records the new requires-python; 'uv lock --check' passes.
4) README.md: state that holon-coherence supports Python 3.13 only, where development setup is described, and that 'uv sync --group dev' creates a 3.13 virtualenv.
5) VERIFY: 'uv sync --group dev' creates a .venv whose interpreter is 3.13; 'uv run task test' and 'uv run task lint' pass; ruff check and format stay clean. If the new target ever required a source change, that change is out of scope: stop and report it.
6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' must pass and every changed Markdown file must pass 'npx prettier --check' (this repository defines no lint-docs task; the requirement is the same check on the changed files, and adding the task is out of scope because pyproject.toml is not in this change's touch set); keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only pyproject.toml, uv.lock, a new .python-version and README.md (in particular .github/workflows/, the Dockerfile, environment.yml, src/ and tests/ are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.question: Is this one intent or should it split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: One intent. It is one interpreter-alignment change across four files.

questions.question: Should CI workflows or the Dockerfile be edited to select 3.13?
questions.answer: No. The workflows rely on uv, which honours .python-version and requires-python; the Dockerfile runs in the mitmproxy base image's own interpreter. Both are outside the touch set, and the workflows belong to a concurrent change.

description: holon-coherence knows about an external harness it must never depend on. Defaults: src/holon_coherence/mitm_addon.py:80 and src/holon_coherence/commands/metrics.py:33 default WIRE_LOG_DIR to 'todo/mitm_wire_logs', and commands/metrics.py:308 appends 'todo/mitm_wire_logs' as a wire-log search directory. .gitignore:36 ignores 'todo/'. Docs point at harness scratch files: docs/methods/README.md:27-35 and docs/methods/*.md reference 'todo/ab_measure_all_methods.py', 'todo/cache', 'todo/openbrain' and 'todo/artifacts/...'; docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md:78-111 runs '../../todo/ab_benchmark_*.py'; docs/token_reduction_measurement_plan.md:85-300 uses 'todo/mitm_wire_logs' and 'todo/cache'; and docs/mitm_telemetry_metrics_plan.md:99-109 links absolute file:///Users/... paths into a harness checkout. External task-tracker ids ('Bean NNNN') appear in docstrings, comments and docs: mitm_addon.py:383,490,558,1119,2005,2020,2211, commands/metrics.py:1,150, commands/endpoints.py:1, commands/start.py:111, metrics_math.py:1, docs/audit_report.md (15 lines), docs/mitm_telemetry_metrics_plan.md:78, and tests/test_ab_testing.py:1, test_cli.py:2490,2650,2859,2889,2920, test_host_local.py:165, test_hybrid_cache.py:1, test_makefile.py:857, test_mitm_addon.py (7 lines) and test_mitm_addon_sse.py:1. No test stops new leaks.
goal:
1) DEFAULTS: change the wire-log default in mitm_addon.py and commands/metrics.py from 'todo/mitm_wire_logs' to the target-native '.holon/mitm_wire_logs' (already ignored through .gitignore's '.holon/' entry), keep the WIRE_LOG_DIR override exactly as it is, and replace the 'todo/mitm_wire_logs' search candidate at metrics.py:308 with the new default. Add a short migration note to the wire-log docs: existing logs under the old directory can be moved or read by setting WIRE_LOG_DIR.
2) GITIGNORE: remove the 'todo/' entry; keep the existing cache, wire-log and '.holon/' entries.
3) DOCS: rewrite every todo/ path in docs/methods/*.md, docs/token_reduction_*.md and docs/mitm_telemetry_metrics_plan.md to a target-native path ('.holon/...' for runtime data, a repository-relative path for anything this repository ships). Where a referenced script does not exist in this repository, describe the measurement instead of linking a file. Remove absolute machine paths. Where a doc shows a test command, use 'uv run pytest'.
4) TASK IDS: replace every 'Bean NNNN' reference in the listed source, test and doc files with a plain description of the behaviour; behaviour stays unchanged. docs/audit_report.md keeps its findings but drops the external ids. Append-only provenance records (holon-knowledge/ledger/*.jsonl, plans/, executions/, intents/) are history and are neither edited nor checked.
5) HYGIENE TEST: add tests/test_repo_hygiene.py (pytest only, reading 'git ls-files' output) that fails when a tracked file lives under todo/, .subagent/ or .beans/, or when a tracked file outside the provenance records contains a todo/ or .subagent/ path, a '.beans/' path, an absolute path into a harness checkout, or a task id matching 'Bean' followed by four digits. Match the directory names exactly, so that a future '.beads/' directory or file is not rejected, and add a test proving that. The repository's own .agents/AGENTS.md is allowed. Build the forbidden patterns so the test file does not match itself. Update affected tests for the new default path.
6) VERIFY: 'git grep' finds no todo/ default or task id outside the provenance records; 'uv run task test' passes.
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' must pass and every changed Markdown file must pass 'npx prettier --check' (this repository defines no lint-docs task; the requirement is the same check on the changed files, and adding the task is out of scope because pyproject.toml is not in this change's touch set); keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only src/holon_coherence/mitm_addon.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/metrics.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/endpoints.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, src/holon_coherence/metrics_math.py, docs/audit_report.md, docs/methods/*.md, docs/mitm_telemetry_metrics_plan.md, docs/token_reduction_*.md, tests/test_mitm_addon*.py, tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_ab_testing.py, tests/test_host_local.py, tests/test_hybrid_cache.py, tests/test_makefile.py, .gitignore and one new tests/test_repo_hygiene.py (in particular .github/workflows/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, README.md, the Makefile and .agents/AGENTS.md are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.question: Is this one intent or should it split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: One intent. Removing the leaks and adding the test that keeps them out belong together; splitting would land a hygiene test that fails on arrival, or removals with no guard.

questions.question: Why a pytest file instead of a check in test-hygiene.yml or pyproject.toml?
questions.answer: Both files belong to concurrent changes. A pytest hygiene test runs in the existing unit job with no workflow edit.

questions.question: Must the hygiene test reject a '.beads/' directory?
questions.answer: No. It must match the forbidden directory names exactly, and a test must prove that '.beads/' passes.

questions.question: Are the ledgers, plans and execution records rewritten to drop old task ids?
questions.answer: No. They are append-only provenance and stay as recorded; the hygiene test excludes them.

description: holon-coherence has no CI timing gate: none of its workflows (docker-build, make, test-hygiene, test-integration, test-unit under .github/workflows/) records or compares job durations, and test-unit.yml runs 'uv sync; uv run task test' (:47) with no per-test timing report, so a slower change reaches main unnoticed. Calibration data (job wall clock, started_at to completed_at, from the GitHub API) for the 16 successful main pushes of 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-24: latest main acbe924 gives unit 53 s ubuntu / 115 s macOS (run 40050933835), integration 79 s (run 40050933935), hygiene 49 s (run 40050933893), make 29 s ubuntu / 50 s macOS (run 40050933865) and docker-build 39 s (run 40050933930); the previous main 29b7e50 gives unit 62 s / 102 s (run 39699387487), integration 81 s (run 39699387340), hygiene 54 s, docker-build 33 s. Ranges over the window: unit ubuntu 49-87 s, unit macOS 73-130 s, integration 67-93 s, hygiene 34-67 s, make ubuntu 29-69 s, make macOS 36-65 s, docker-build 25-63 s. Against the median of the previous 5 runs the worst healthy deviations were +38 % / +24 s (unit ubuntu), +31 % / +22 s (integration) and +28 % / +26 s (unit macOS). Replaying a rolling median of 5 with a 50 % tolerance and a 30 s minimum absolute delta flags none of these runs.
goal:
1) RECORD: on every successful push to main, each CI job (every job in every workflow under .github/workflows/, including the image-build jobs) records its wall-clock duration (from a timestamp taken in the job's first step to the gate step at its end), the job name and the runner OS; test jobs also record pytest's per-test durations through a '--junitxml=<path>' flag added to the test command in the workflow file (not in pyproject.toml or the Makefile). Store the record as a workflow artefact named per job and OS, never in the repository and never as a ledger.
2) COMPARE: on a pull request each job compares its duration with the rolling median of the last N successful main records for the same job and OS, fetched read-only with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (grant 'actions: read' only where it is needed). While fewer than N records exist (cold start, or a job that has never run on main) the relative check is skipped with an explicit notice and only the ceiling applies.
3) FAIL: the job fails only when its duration exceeds the baseline median by more than the relative tolerance AND by more than the minimum absolute delta. Defaults, calibrated from the real runs cited in the description: N = 5, tolerance = 50 %, minimum absolute delta = 30 s.
4) EXPLAIN: test jobs compare per-test times with the baseline median and name the top 10 tests whose time grew by more than 50 % and more than 5 s; this report is printed on every pull-request run and appended to the failure message, and does not fail the job on its own.
5) CEILING: every job also fails above an absolute ceiling of 300 s, whatever the baseline. 300 s passes every job on today's main (the largest job in the whole window is 130 s, unit macos-latest) with more than double headroom.
6) OVERRIDE: a pull-request label 'timing-regression-accepted' turns a relative-check failure into a printed warning that names the label, so every override is visible on the pull request. The ceiling cannot be overridden by label; it changes only through a committed edit to its flag in the workflow file.
7) CONFIGURATION: N, the tolerance, the minimum delta and the ceiling are command-line flags of the script, set in the workflow commands, never in pyproject.toml or the Makefile.
8) SCRIPT AND TESTS: a single new module scripts/ci_timing_gate.py (standard library only; network and artefact access behind small injectable functions) and tests/test_ci_timing_gate.py (pytest only, with fake fetchers; never real network, gh or GitHub API calls). Cover: rolling median; pass inside the tolerance; fail only when both the tolerance and the minimum delta are exceeded; the ceiling; cold start below N; label override of the relative check but not the ceiling; the per-test top-offender report; JUnit parsing; and a replay of the real durations cited in the description showing that the most recent main runs pass.
9) DOCS: document the gate, its defaults and why they were chosen, how to read the report and how to accept a deliberate slow-down in .github/workflows/README.md.
10) This repository is independent: write its own script; do not import from or refer to any other repository.
11) Pushing workflow-file changes requires a token with the 'workflow' scope; if the execution branch push is refused for that reason, report it as a blocker rather than dropping the workflow edits.
12) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' must pass and every changed Markdown file must pass 'npx prettier --check' (this repository defines no lint-docs task; the requirement is the same check on the changed files, and adding the task is out of scope because pyproject.toml is not in this change's touch set); keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only .github/workflows/*.yml, .github/workflows/README.md, the new scripts/ci_timing_gate.py and the new tests/test_ci_timing_gate.py (in particular pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version, README.md, src/, the Makefile and every other test file are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.question: Is this one intent or should it split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: One intent. Recording, comparison, explanation, ceiling and override form one gate in one script and the workflows that call it.

questions.question: Why a 30 s floor here when a sibling project uses a larger one?
questions.answer: Calibrated on this repository's own main runs: its jobs are short (25-130 s) and comparatively steady, so 50 % plus 30 s catches a real doubling of any test job while no healthy run in the window would have failed.

questions.question: May the gate add pytest-xdist or change the test task?
questions.answer: No. No new dependencies, and pyproject.toml belongs to a concurrent change; add the JUnit flag to the command in the workflow file only.

questions.question: Must the ceiling pass today's main?
questions.answer: Yes. 300 s clears every job on acbe924 and on the whole recent main window.

description: Enable Ruff cyclomatic and structural complexity rules (C901, PLR0911, PLR0912, PLR0913, PLR0915) in pyproject.toml with thresholds matching holon-agentic-coder (mccabe.max-complexity = 10, pylint max-returns = 6, max-branches = 12, max-args = 5, max-statements = 50), baseline the existing violating functions strictly via inline # noqa comments (via ruff check --add-noqa, never per-file-ignores), add a pytest ratchet test in tests/test_complexity_baseline.py, and document the complexity gate thresholds and ratchet policy in docs/token_reduction_architecture.md.
rationale: holon-coherence currently enables only select = ["E", "F", "I", "W"] in pyproject.toml with no cyclomatic or structural complexity gate, allowing 38 functions across src/holon_coherence/ to grow up to C901 = 68 and 183 statements (such as HolonCoherenceAddon.response and build_proxy_status_report) without any automated lint gate. Enabling C901 and PLR0911-PLR0915 with inline # noqa comments on existing violations and a ceiling ratchet test prevents any new or touched function from exceeding the thresholds while keeping existing debt visible at each call site.
acceptance_criteria: In pyproject.toml, extend [tool.ruff.lint] select to include "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", and "PLR0915", and add [tool.ruff.lint.mccabe] max-complexity = 10 and [tool.ruff.lint.pylint] max-args = 5, max-branches = 12, max-returns = 6, max-statements = 50.

Baseline the existing violating functions in src/holon_coherence/ strictly via inline # noqa: <RULE> comments on the specific def lines (using uv run ruff check --add-noqa src/ tests/ or equivalent targeted inline comments). Do NOT add C901, PLR0911, PLR0912, PLR0913, or PLR0915 toignore or per-file-ignores in pyproject.toml.

Do NOT refactor the existing violating functions in this change; keep the diff strictly to pyproject.toml, inline # noqa comments on existing violations, tests/test_complexity_baseline.py, and docs/token_reduction_architecture.md. Do NOT touch docs/methods/README.md or docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md.

Add tests/test_complexity_baseline.py that verifies pyproject.toml configures C901 and PLR0911-PLR0915 with the exact thresholds, asserts neither ignore nor per-file-ignores suppresses those rules, runs ruff check passes cleanly, and enforces a ratchet ceiling on the count of inline # noqa comments referencing C901/PLR0911/PLR0912/PLR0913/PLR0915 across src/holon_coherence/ so the baseline count can only decrease over time.
Document the complexity thresholds and inline # noqa ratchet policy in docs/token_reduction_architecture.md using Australian English (en-AU).
uv run ruff check src/ tests/, uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/, and uv run pytest pass with zero errors.

description: Extract the duplicated CI Timing Gate (Start) and CI Timing Gate (Check <= 5 min) steps across all 5 GitHub Actions workflows into a single local composite action at .github/actions/ci-timing-gate/action.yml with a phase input (start | check), and update all 5 workflows and .github/workflows/README.md to use it.
rationale: All 5 workflows in .github/workflows/ (docker-build.yml, make.yml, test-hygiene.yml, test-integration.yml, test-unit.yml) repeat the exact same two shell steps at the start and end of every job to record CI_JOB_START_EPOCH and run scripts/check_ci_runtime_budget.py. Extracting these steps into a single local composite action at .github/actions/ci-timing-gate/action.yml with phase: start and phase: check eliminates the 10-step duplication across workflows while keeping both steps in one self-contained action file.
acceptance_criteria: Create .github/actions/ci-timing-gate/action.yml as a composite action with required input phase (start or check) and optional input max-seconds (default '300').
When inputs.phase == 'start', the composite action writes CI_JOB_START_EPOCH=$(date +%s) to $GITHUB_ENV using shell: bash.

When inputs.phase == 'check', the composite action runs python3 "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/scripts/check_ci_runtime_budget.py" --start-epoch "${CI_JOB_START_EPOCH}" --max-seconds "${{ inputs.max-seconds }}" --step-summary "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}" using shell: bash.
Add a validation step in .github/actions/ci-timing-gate/action.yml that fails with a clear error message if inputs.phase is neither 'start' nor 'check'.

Update all 5 workflows (docker-build.yml, make.yml, test-hygiene.yml, test-integration.yml, test-unit.yml) to replace the inline CI Timing Gate (Start) and CI Timing Gate (Check <= 5 min) run blocks with uses: ./.github/actions/ci-timing-gate and with: phase: start / phase: check (preserving if: always() on the check step and ordering check_out before phase: start so ./.github/actions/ci-timing-gate is available on disk).
Update .github/workflows/README.md to document .github/actions/ci-timing-gate/action.yml.
All existing tests including uv run pytest tests/test_ci_timing_gate.py and uv run pytest pass with zero failures.

description: Update the live-command A/B test documentation recipes in docs/methods/README.md and docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md so that (1) the manual mitmdump command is started in a separate terminal or backgrounded with a readiness check before running ab-test --command, and (2) the 'Inspect live cumulative totals' step in the two-pass container workflow clearly explains that CumulativeMetrics resets on proxy restart and points to ab-test --trace-file for the paired baseline-vs-optimised scorecard.
rationale: In docs/methods/README.md and docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md, the host-side mitmdump command is shown as a foreground command in the same shell block immediately before holon-coherence ab-test --command, which blocks the shell so the second command never executes as written (and a bare '&' is insufficient because set_proxy_mode() returns False silently if the proxy is not yet listening). Additionally, in docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md, the two-pass container workflow shows holon-coherence metrics --json after holon-coherence stop && holon-coherence start -d without noting that CumulativeMetrics is in-memory and resets on proxy restart, so metrics --json after restart reflects only the second pass whereas ab-test --trace-file ~/.holon/logs/transactions.jsonl reads both passes from the append-only log.
acceptance_criteria: In docs/methods/README.md (around lines 29-39) and docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md (around lines 120-130), update the 'Option B: Run mitmdump manually on the host' / 'Option 2: Live Command Execution (--command)' recipe so mitmdump is either started in a separate terminal or started in the background with an explicit readiness wait (polling http://127.0.0.1:8080/__holon__/health or ~/.holon/control/status) before running uv run holon-coherence ab-test --command.

In docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md (around lines 105-115), update the '5. Inspect live cumulative totals' step after 'holon-coherence stop && holon-coherence start -d' to state clearly that in-memory CumulativeMetrics resets when the proxy restarts (so metrics --json after step 3 reports only the optimised pass unless captured before stop as well), and point to holon-coherence ab-test --trace-file ~/.holon/logs/transactions.jsonl for the paired baseline-vs-optimised scorecard across both passes.
Do NOT modify pyproject.toml, src/, or .github/ workflows in this change; keep the diff strictly scoped to docs/methods/README.md and docs/token_reduction_ab_testing.md.
Use Australian English (en-AU) spelling and pass uv run pytest and npx prettier --check.

description: Refactor holon-coherence command modules so each command in src/holon_coherence/commands/ registers its own subparser via register(subparsers) and handles invocation via handle(args), removing the sys.modules dynamic locator in _dispatch.py and decoupling cli.py and tests/test_cli.py.
rationale: In holon-coherence, cli.main defines every subparser inline (349 lines, CC 31) and command handlers look up collaborators through commands/_dispatch.get_cli() (a sys.modules dynamic lookup used 15 times in 8 modules). This couples every command and test to cli.py (286 patch targets in test_cli.py). Moving registration and handling into each command module allows cli.main to become a slim dispatcher and enables splitting test_cli.py cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: Each command module in src/holon_coherence/commands/ exports register(subparsers) and handle(args) functions.
cli.main discovers or registers the command modules explicitly and dispatches to them in a concise entrypoint function.
Remove src/holon_coherence/commands/_dispatch.py and eliminate all sys.modules service locator lookups.
Command modules receive collaborators explicitly as function/constructor arguments with sensible defaults, enabling clean injection without circular imports.
Split tests/test_cli.py into modular tests under tests/commands/test_<command>.py while maintaining or increasing total test count.
Ensure all touched and refactored functions comply with the ruff complexity limits established in Bean 0186 (C901 <= 10, etc.).
All test suites pass using 'uv run pytest' with zero failures.
